## Polished idea

**Problem:** Owners miss early signs of illness in senior dogs until treatment is costly.

**Solution:** A smart collar and app that track activity and vitals and alert owners early.

**Target users:** City owners of dogs aged eight and older.

**Value proposition:** Peace of mind from earlier detection at a fraction of vet-bill cost.

**Key assumptions**

- Owners will pay monthly
- Sensors are accurate enough

**Variants**

- Vet partnership channel

**Claims**

- Senior dogs need frequent health monitoring. [1]

## Market

**TAM:** $4.2B — Top-down from pet care spend ([source](https://example.com/pet-market))
**SAM:** $900M — Urban senior-dog owners ([source](https://example.com/pet-market))
**SOM:** $20M — 1 percent of SAM in year three

Cheap sensors make this possible now. ([source](https://example.com/pet-market))

## Competitors

| Competitor | Positioning | Pricing | Gap |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [VetTrack](https://example.com/vettrack-pricing) | Vet-first monitoring | $40/month | No consumer self-serve track for early alerts |
| [PawSense](https://example.com/pawsense) | Activity tracking only | $25/month | No health signals beyond steps |

**Differentiation:** The consumer wedge is early alerts without a vet visit. ([source](https://example.com/vettrack-pricing))

## Feasibility

- **Technical:** Sensor firmware plus a companion mobile app.
- **Operational:** Support, replacements, and firmware updates.
- **Legal / regulatory:** Consumer device and privacy rules apply.
- **MVP cost:** $40k-$70k
- **MVP timeline:** 4-6 months

### Risks

| Risk | Likelihood | Impact | Mitigation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Sensor accuracy | 3/5 | 4/5 | Bench test against veterinary data |
| Battery life | 2/5 | 3/5 | Use low-power firmware profile |

### Claims

- Consumer health devices need privacy review. _(unverified: source unavailable)_
